name: Plumbing & Drainage (Domestic Water, Soil/Waste/Vent, Storm) Installation, Flushing, Testing & Disinfection

activities: below-ground drainage trenches excavated to gradient
underslab drainage laid, bedded and connected to manholes before slab pour
floor/wall sleeves and puddle flanges cast in for risers and penetrations
tank room slab / plinth and bund poured
builder's openings for stacks and rainwater pipes formed
wet-area floor falls and waterproofing tanking coordinated
sequence.note: Below-ground drainage is captive to civil sequencing — it must be laid, tested and inspected before the slab is poured over it; sleeves and puddle flanges must be cast in, not cut later.

activities: gravity drainage runs laid to gradient with correct falls
connection to manholes / inspection chambers / septic or municipal
bedding and surround before backfill
sequence.note: Falls/gradient are critical for gravity drainage; laid and tested before cover.

activities: air/water (hydrostatic) test of underground drainage
CCTV / visual inspection of gradient and joints before backfill
sign-off before slab pour or backfill
sequence.note: Drainage test and inspection MUST precede backfill/slab — a buried untested run is uninspectable later.

activities: soil/waste/vent stacks erected in risers with supports and fire-collars
storm/rainwater downpipes erected
domestic cold/hot water risers erected with supports
branch drainage and water branches roughed into wet walls and ceiling voids
fire-stopping collars at rated floor penetrations
sequence.note: Vertical stacks and risers first, then horizontal branches; drainage graded, water pipe supported and sloped for drain-down.

activities: water storage tanks set in tank room
booster / transfer pump sets set and aligned on plinths
hot water calorifiers / heaters / plate heat exchangers set
pressure vessels and dosing set
sequence.note: Plant is set on cured plinths; pump sets follow rotating-equipment practice (alignment before piped connection).

activities: hydrostatic pressure test of domestic cold and hot water piping by section, witnessed
hold and inspect for leaks before concealment
air/water test of above-ground soil and waste (or gravity fill test on stacks)
sequence.note: Pressure/leak test BEFORE ceilings close, wet walls are boarded, and before insulation.

activities: flush domestic water system to remove debris, swarf and flux
clear strainers and check for cleanliness
sequence.note: Flushing requires the pressure test passed and the distribution complete to fixtures/outlets.

activities: chlorinate / disinfect the potable water system to standard
dwell, then flush to residual and normal levels
take water samples for bacteriological (potability) test
sequence.note: Disinfection follows flushing and precedes handover of a potable system; sampling proves potability.

activities: hot water and cold water (anti-condensation) pipe insulation
trace-heating where specified for DHW / freeze protection
fire-rated wrap where required
sequence.note: Insulation follows a passed pressure test; concealed pipe insulated after testing.

activities: sanitary fixtures set: WCs, basins, sinks, urinals, showers
traps, connectors, angle valves and flush mechanisms fitted
floor gullies, roof drains and cleanouts finalised
tap/mixer and appliance connections made
sequence.note: Fixtures follow tiling/wet-wall finishes and ceiling completion; the last wet trade in a finished space.

activities: booster pump, calorifier, trace-heating and water-heater power feeds terminated
level switches, flow, temperature sensors and controls wired
leak-detection and BMS points landed
sequence.note: Pump/heater plant requires power and controls; requires containment + cabling complete.

activities: pump solo run, rotation, alignment and duty/standby check
tank fill, float/level switch and overflow verification
calorifier / water-heater setpoint and safety (T&P valve) checks
BMS point verification for plant
sequence.note: Pump and heater plant proven before full-flow commissioning; safety devices verified first.

activities: set booster pump duty pressure and duty/standby/alternation sequence
verify flow and pressure at the most remote/highest fixtures
hot water circulation temperature and dead-leg / anti-legionella verification
drainage flow / discharge and trap-seal retention test with fixtures live
integrated controls test with BMS (levels, leak, temperature)
sequence.note: Final commissioning proves pressure and hot-water temperature at the worst-case fixture and drainage performance with fixtures connected; depends on live power, filled tanks, disinfected potable water and BMS.

typical_relationships.before: Underground drainage laid, tested and inspected
typical_relationships.reason: Buried drainage cannot be inspected or corrected after the slab is poured; test and sign-off must precede cover.

typical_relationships.before: Drainage laid to correct falls / gradient
typical_relationships.reason: A gravity run must be complete and correctly graded before it can hold a test and be inspected.

typical_relationships.before: Soil/waste/vent stacks and water risers erected
typical_relationships.after: Horizontal branch connections in ceiling voids / wet walls
typical_relationships.reason: Branches tie into the vertical stacks and risers, which must exist and be supported first.

typical_relationships.before: Domestic water piping pressure test passed
typical_relationships.after: Pipe insulation and wet-wall / ceiling closure
typical_relationships.reason: Concealing or insulating pipe before a leak test forces demolition to reach a later leak.
Flushing an un-proven system risks leaks under flow; prove integrity before running water through it.
Debris and biofilm must be flushed out before disinfection, otherwise the potability sample can fail.

typical_relationships.before: Wet-wall finishes / tiling and ceilings complete
typical_relationships.reason: Fixtures are set against finished walls/floors and are the last wet trade; installing before finishes causes rework and damage.
Rated penetrations for combustible drainage stacks require intumescent collars fitted before the barrier is signed off.

typical_relationships.before: Booster pump power and controls terminated and meggered
typical_relationships.reason: A pump motor cannot be run for rotation/duty check until its feeder and protection are connected and insulation-tested.

typical_relationships.before: Tanks filled and disinfected; pumps running
typical_relationships.after: Booster pressure and remote-fixture flow commissioning
typical_relationships.reason: Duty pressure and worst-case fixture flow can only be set with a filled, disinfected system and pumps operating.
Trap-seal loss and drainage performance are tested by discharging the actual fixtures, which must be connected first.

typical_relationships.before: Hot water generation and circulation running
typical_relationships.reason: Circulation return temperatures and dead-leg temperatures can only be proven once DHW is generated and circulating.

interfaces.requirement: Underslab drainage trenches, cast-in sleeves and puddle flanges, tank-room plinths/bunds, wet-area falls and waterproofing must be ready before underground drainage, riser erection and plant setting.
Incoming mains water supply and connection to municipal/site sewer and storm networks must be live to fill, flush and commission the system.
Booster pumps, water heaters/calorifiers and trace-heating require power feeders energised before pre-commissioning and commissioning.
Power and control cabling to plumbing plant requires containment installed and cables pulled and terminated first.
Tank levels, leak detection, DHW temperature and pump status points must be BMS-verified for integrated control and alarms.
Booster/transfer pump sets follow rotating-equipment practice: alignment and grouting before piped connection.
Hot/cold water pipe insulation is applied only after the pressure test passes.
Wet-riser / plumbing risers and sprinkler pipe often share shafts and ceiling voids; routing and penetrations must be coordinated to avoid clashes and duplicated fire-stopping.
Level switches, flow and temperature sensors, and leak-detection must be installed and verified before plant pre-commissioning.
Riser and stack supports rely on structural inserts/steel and shaft framing being available.

testing_requirements: Underground drainage air/water test and CCTV / visual inspection before backfill or slab pour
Hydrostatic pressure test of domestic cold and hot water piping by section, witnessed, before concealment
Disinfection / chlorination of potable system with bacteriological (potability) sample pass
Pump-motor insulation resistance (megger) test before energisation
Booster pump duty/standby/alternation and duty-pressure functional test
Flow and pressure verification at the most remote / highest fixture
Hot water circulation temperature and anti-legionella / dead-leg verification
Drainage discharge and trap-seal retention test with fixtures connected
Tank overflow, float/level switch and leak-detection verification
commissioning_dependencies: Incoming water main and sewer/storm connections live
Permanent (or commissioning) power to booster pumps, water heaters and trace-heating
Tanks filled; potable system flushed and disinfected with a passed potability sample
Domestic water piping pressure-tested and drainage tested/inspected before concealment/backfill
Sanitary fixtures installed (after finishes) so drainage and worst-case fixture flow can be tested
BMS/controls live for tank levels, leak detection and DHW temperature
Instrumentation and safety devices (T&P valves, level switches) installed and verified
Below-ground drainage signed off before slab pour (captive to civil sequence)

work_packages.wp: Soil/waste/vent and rainwater stacks and branches

work_packages.note: interfaces with civil bases and rotating_equipment

work_packages.wp: Plumbing plant power and control termination

typical_exceptions: Gravity-fed systems from a high-level storage tank omit booster pumps, dropping the pump alignment and duty-pressure stages.
Instantaneous / point-of-use water heaters replace central calorifiers, removing DHW circulation and dead-leg stages.
Rainwater/storm-only scopes have no potable disinfection or fixture stages.
Small tenant fit-outs connect to existing base-build risers, so riser erection and plant setting do not apply.
Where drainage is pumped (below sewer level), a packaged lifting/sump station adds an electrical and float-control commissioning step to an otherwise gravity system.
evidence: Below-ground drainage is scheduled to be covered by the slab before its air/water test and inspection, potable disinfection/sampling is scheduled before flushing (or before the system is complete to outlets), pipe is insulated or wet walls are closed before the witnessed pressure test, or booster-pressure/fixture-flow commissioning is set before tanks are filled and the system disinfected.
